newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sees sugar imports in 1997/1998.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sees sugar imports in 1997/1998.

text.p: The Philippines is expected to return to overseas sugar markets in the 1997-1998 crop year ending August 31 to meet a projected production shortfall of nearly 500,000 tonnes, the state-run Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) said on Wednesday.
"We may likely go back to the import market in 1997/1998," SRA administrator Wilson Gamboa said.
Gamboa said he expected imports in addition to the 45,000 tonnes of purchases stipulated by the World Trade Organisation for crop year 1997-1998.

Sugar output in 1997/1998 is expected to drop to 1.7 million tonnes from the revised forecast of 1.8 million in the current crop year because farmers are switching to other crops on the back of a current glut, the SRA has said.
Gamboa said he expected the current sugar glut, blamed on high production and over importation, to be mopped up by the market by August this year.

In 1997-1998, total sugar available is expected at 2.123 million tonnes, including production, compulsory imports and inventories, while demand was placed at 2.25-2.26 million tonnes, including 250,000 tonnes in sugar exports to the United States.

Gamboa said he expected a shortfall of between 477,000-487,000 tonnes in 1997-1998 given the required buffer of around 350,000 tonnes at the end of the crop year and the projected demand-supply gap of 127,000-137,000 tonnes.
